verdicts.reason: A: the SOLSTICE wordmark sits under the headline, which flips the reading order. The headline and subhead run almost to both canvas edges, and the three flavour pills have random widths (Honey Rosemary is huge, Blood Orange is tiny), but the Shop Flavours button stays strong at the bottom. B: the pills are scattered at different x positions, Cucumber Mint floats alone and centred, and the Shop Flavours button is shrunk into the bottom-left corner, so the CTA is buried.

A has the same flaws as pair 1: the brand sits below the headline, the pill widths look arbitrary and the margins are tight, but the headline and CTA are clearly prominent. B lets three oversized pills on the left dominate. The subhead on the right is shrunk to illegible size, the headline jams against the right edge and the CTA is small, so the hierarchy is inverted.

A: the brand is below the headline, the pills are inconsistently sized and the copy runs edge to edge, but every label is readable. B has a cleaner two-column layout and a strong CTA, but the pill labels are shrunk to roughly 5px and can't be read. The CTA also crowds into the peach circle and the headline hugs the right edge.

A: the brand is below the headline and the pill widths are mismatched, but the CTA closes the reading order strongly at the bottom. B has evenly sized, centred pills, but the Shop Flavours button is tiny and floats above the headline, which breaks the reading order and buries the CTA. The large pills then compete as the main focal point.
